_comment: Hand-maintained register of every tracked exception/finding this repository carries, cross-referenced with the machine-generated secreport.json/vex.json (cmd/secreport). Update this file in the same PR that changes an exception's scope or review date.

entries.title: 5 remaining npm audit findings (low only) in website/ (Docusaurus dev-tooling deps) -- reduced from 26 on 2026-11-14
entries.affected_component: website/package-lock.json: deepmerge, @svgr/plugin-svgo, @svgr/webpack, @docusaurus/plugin-svgr, @docusaurus/preset-classic (SVG-handling chain only -- tinypool, webpack-dev-server/sockjs/uuid, serialize-javascript, copy-webpack-plugin, and css-minimizer-webpack-plugin were fixed, see remediation)
entries.fixed_version: none safe for the remaining 5 -- deepmerge has no patched release at all (its vulnerable range >=4.2.0 covers every version up to and including the latest, 4.3.1, confirmed via `npm view deepmerge versions`); npm's only suggested fix for the rest of the chain is `--force`-installing an OLDER @docusaurus/preset-classic (3.6.3, a downgrade from the pinned 3.10.2, isSemVerMajor: true), rejected for the same reason as the original investigation
entries.exploitability_context: build/dev-tooling only (npm start, docusaurus build) -- none of the affected packages ship in website/build/, the deployed static site
entries.environment: local development and CI build tooling, not the published site
entries.remediation: 2026-11-14: fixed 21 of 26 findings (including all 16 critical and the 1 high) via three targeted package.json `overrides` -- tinypool (1.1.1 -> 2.2.0), serialize-javascript (6.0.2 -> 7.1.4), uuid (8.3.2 -> 11.1.1) -- verified compatible (npm install + docusaurus build + link check all pass unchanged, no --force used). The remaining 5 (deepmerge and its dependents, all low severity) have no available fix; next step is a dedicated Docusaurus major-version migration or removing/replacing the @svgr SVG-handling path, as its own reviewable change
entries.status: open, tracked. Closed and reopened twice on 2026-11-13, each time without a linked remediation PR: first closed ~12:45, reopened ~13:03 after re-verification (live CI re-check, PR #45: 26 findings, matching this entry's then-current severity breakdown); closed again ~18:41, reopened again after a second re-verification (fresh npm audit: still 26 findings, identical breakdown both times). The count above (5, all low) reflects a REAL fix applied 2026-11-14 (see remediation), not a change in issue-tracker state -- website/.security/npm-audit-baseline.json has been updated to this new baseline and still gates on it in CI. This status is not a claim that the remaining 5 are resolved.

entries.title: Python base-image OS-package CVEs -- 0 HIGH/CRITICAL remaining as of 2026-11-14 (was 98, 2 critical)
entries.affected_component: apps/python-api's runtime image base -- moved python:3.12-slim-bookworm -> python:3.12-slim-trixie -> python:3.12-alpine across this investigation (2026-11-14). The 5 remaining MEDIUM/1 LOW are pip's own package metadata, still present in the copied site-packages (not a runtime dependency, not shipped as a console-script binary) -- a candidate follow-up, not an actionable HIGH/CRITICAL finding
entries.fixed_version: krb5-libs 1.22.3-r0 and zlib 1.4-r0 (both applied, cleared the base image's last 16 HIGH findings). The 5 remaining MEDIUM pip findings have fixes upstream (pip 25.3/26.1/26.1.2/26.2.0) but pip itself is no longer copied into the runtime image at all as of this fix, pending confirmation its dist-info metadata is also excludable
entries.exploitability_context: No HIGH/CRITICAL findings remain to assess reachability for. The residual pip metadata is not a runtime dependency (the pip console script is excluded; only its package metadata lingers in the copied site-packages)
entries.evidence: unfiltered Trivy scan against the final built image (python:3.12-alpine, krb5-libs/zlib upgraded, pip binary excluded): 0 HIGH, 0 CRITICAL, 5 MEDIUM, 1 LOW, reproducible via `trivy image <image>` (no severity filter, no ignore-unfixed) -- the CI gate (`ignore-unfixed` exception removed entirely, see python-ci.yml) now runs at the full HIGH,CRITICAL threshold with nothing suppressed
entries.remediation: 2026-11-14, three steps, each verified compatible before switching (full test suite, ruff, mypy, a real build/run, /healthz unchanged at every step): (1) bookworm -> trixie: 98 findings (2 critical) -> 47 (0 critical). (2) trixie -> alpine: re-tested the F3 distroless/Alpine rejection (docs/adr/0004) -- musllinux wheels now exist on PyPI for pydantic_core/uvloop/httptools/watchfiles (none existed when F3 rejected this), so no compiler is needed; base-image findings dropped to 16 HIGH, 0 critical. (3) `apk upgrade krb5-libs=1.22.3-r0 zlib=1.4-r0` cleared all 16. Also stopped copying pip/mypy/ruff/pytest and other dev-only tooling into the runtime image (only the uvicorn binary is copied), which incidentally removes most of the residual low-severity findings too. Next step, if any: investigate excluding pip's dist-info metadata from the copied site-packages to clear the last 5 MEDIUM/1 LOW.
entries.status: effectively resolved for HIGH/CRITICAL as of 2026-11-14 (0 remaining, down from 98) -- the GitHub issue itself has not been closed by this change; that is a separate decision requiring explicit approval, not made here. Prior history: closed and reopened twice on 2026-11-13, each time without a linked remediation PR, after re-verification showed the then-current 98 findings still present both times. This entry's prior reduction (98 -> 47, trixie) is superseded by this one (-> 0, alpine); nothing about either prior record is deleted, only superseded by a later, more complete fix.
